Figure 1 | Sequential stages during the genetic transformation of common bean plants. (a) Seedlings are
germinated for 2 days on paper towels. (b) Seedlings are planted into pots with vermiculite. (c) Five-day-
old seedlings, with unfolded cotyledons, are shown just before A. rhizogenes infection. (d) Bacterial
suspension preparation: Agrobacterium is collected with a glass rod from the Petri dish edge, and
bacterial suspension is placed in an Eppendorf tube. (e) Infection with the bacterial suspension into the
cotyledonary node zone. Stereo-micrographs of (f) calli formed at wounded sites and (g) hairy roots
emerging from infected sites. (h) Plant with hairy roots, 12 days after infection with A. rhizogenes.
(i) Plant transplanted into a new pot; hairy roots tend to grow over the vermiculite surface. (j) Composite
plant with nodulated roots, 3 weeks after inoculation with Rhizobium. (k) A transgenic root expressing
a double tandem tomato construct (tdT)13 was visualized by laser scanning confocal microscopy
(see MATERIALS). Fresh roots were mounted with 1:1 (v/v) PBS/glycerol for detection, and tdT excitation
was performed at 554 nm using a He/Ne laser and a main dichroic beam splitter HFT UV 488/543/633 nm
with a BP 565–615 IR emission ﬁlter. (l) PSN30GFP-GUS expression in P. vulgaris c.v. Negro Jamapa
transgenic root nodules section was observed by laser scanning confocal microscopy (see MATERIALS).
PSN30 fused to the GFP-GUS reporter protein expression was driven by the CaMV35S promoter. Micrograph
showing the central zone of the nodule was observed at 40. The localization of the PSN30GFP-GUS
fusion protein is indicated by arrows. Abbreviations: ic, infected cells; e, epidermis; c, cortex. The
root-nodule section was processed by ﬁxation-dehydration, embedding and sectioning as previously
described by Estrada-Navarrete et al.12. For detection, the tissue was mounted with Citiﬂuor and GFP
excitation was performed at 488 nm using an Ar 2 laser and a main dichroic beam splitter HFT UV
488/543/633 nm with an LP 505 nm emission ﬁlter. Simultaneously, autoﬂuorescence (data not shown)
was observed by exciting at 543 nm with a He/Ne laser, with the same main dichroic beam splitter
and an LP 560 nm emission ﬁlter as described by Van Lent J.W. (2006; Imaging GFP and plant
autoﬂuorescence–Multitracking. Carl Zeiss Microscopy Brochure, Jena, Germany; http://www.zeiss.de/
C1256D18002CC306/Order?OpenForm&lsm-bio). Adobe Photoshop 7.0 software (Adobe Systems Inc.)
was used to process images.
